Senses.Explanation: Travel on foot means to journey from place to place on one's own feet. Chan records use the expression for departing an instructor or monastery, crossing the various regions, and seeking other teachers. Dongshan Liangjie asks permission to travel and is directed toward Nanquan; Yaoshan Weiyan asks whether a visitor has travelled through the regions seeking what is hard to obtain. Later records speak of travelling a thousand miles to seek a lineage teacher and of a 'person travelling on foot' (行腳人) or 'patch-robed monk travelling on foot' (衲僧行腳). The walking journey is literal; whom the traveller visits and what is asked belong to each encounter.
Senses.Note: The corpus also turns the activity into a test. Asked "What is the affair of traveling on foot?" (如何是行腳事), Poshan answers, "face to face, looking at one another, the mouth is like wood" (面面相看口如木). Another instruction calls someone who has passed through a cited exchange a "true person traveling on foot" (真行腳人). No formula in the corpus makes the term a separate prescribed system.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是行腳事？」師云：「面面相看口如木。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄): an unnamed monk is the exact questioner asking about the business of traveling on foot; Poshan Haiming is the respondent and record owner.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: the unnamed monk asking about traveling on foot

Occurrences.Kwic: 某甲欲得行腳，乞和尚處分。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Dongshan Liangjie biography: Dongshan asks his teacher Wuxie for permission to travel on foot; Wuxie directs him to seek Nanquan Puyuan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汝諸方行腳來覓取難得底物來不？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Yaoshan Weiyan section: Yaoshan asks an unnamed visitor whether he has travelled through the various regions seeking the hard-to-obtain thing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖則千里行腳，為尋宗師
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shanhui (山暉禪師語錄): Shanhui says that travelling a thousand miles is done to seek a lineage teacher, then criticizes travellers who still cannot swallow what is offered.

Occurrences.Kwic: 於此透過方是真行腳人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Zhuanyu Heng at Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄): Zhuanyu Heng says that passing through here makes a genuine person travelling on foot.

Occurrences.Kwic: 黃檗和尚示眾云：『汝等盡是噇酒糟漢，恁麼行腳取笑於人，還知大唐國裏無禪師麼？』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Rain Mountain Record (雨山和尚語錄) explicitly introduces a quotation from Huangbo Xiyun; Huangbo rebukes his assembly for traveling on foot only to invite ridicule.

Occurrences.Kwic: 陳操尚書請雲門齋，纔見便問：『儒書中即不問，三乘十二分教自有座主，作麼生是衲僧行腳事？』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tianyin Record (天隱和尚語錄) quotes the explicitly named minister Chen Cao asking Yunmen about the business of a patch-robed monk traveling on foot.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The expanded quoted exchange explicitly names the lay interlocutor before this headword-bearing question.
